worst_three.where: And the hardest hit were chip companies
worst_three.problem: About 150 words of politics, polls and two long quotes run without a breath, so the listener loses the thread before the 'what this means' turn.
worst_three.fix: Insert [Pause] after 'renting out computing power for AI.' and after 'Michigan and Texas.' Split the NBC line: 'NBC News ran an exit poll. More than half of voters said data centers were a major or deciding factor in their vote for Congress. [Pause]' Shorten Austin: 'Maura Austin studies behavioral science at the University of Virginia. She told CNBC people don't want a data center next door if it only makes a big tech company richer. [Pause] And a trillion-dollar listing, she says, puts Anthropic right in that big-tech image.'

worst_three.problem: Right after describing Point2, 'it' sounds like Point2 is the investor, which misleads the listener about who is funding the three startups.
worst_three.fix: Rewrite as: 'And NVIDIA says it plans to invest in three more Korean startups: a model lab in Seoul, a robotics company, and a maker of language models and document tools. [Pause]' Also change 'It also announced work with SK Telecom' to 'NVIDIA also announced work with SK Telecom and the chipmaker Rebellions.'

worst_three.problem: Only two partners were named, so 'the third partner' sounds like a translation slip and leaves the listener unsure who built the wallet.
worst_three.fix: Merge into one natural line: 'OpenAI built it with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, and users keep their card points and protections.' Then add [Pause] before 'And most importantly, according to OpenAI…' to break the 120-word run in the how-it-works section.
